userStories.title: Add typed issue schema (stage/status/blockedBy/wsjf?/rank?/spec?) + issues.schema.json
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I need a single typed source of truth for the issue lifecycle so that every reader/writer of issues.local.json shares one shape and a JSON-schema validation oracle exists, replacing the ad-hoc state+priority fields.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/issues/types.ts exports the enum types `IssueStage = 'idea' | 'specified' | 'planned' | 'shipped'` and `IssueStatus = 'open' | 'abandoned'`, plus the `IssueEntry` interface with required `id: string`, `title: string`, `stage: IssueStage`, `status: IssueStatus`, `blockedBy: string[]`, `createdAt: string`, and optional `description?`, `wsjf?: { value: number; timeCriticality: number; riskReduction: number; jobSize: number }`, `rank?: number`, `spec?: unknown`; and the `IssuesLocalJson` interface `{ next_id: number; issues: IssueEntry[] }`. [oracle: grep -Eq "export type IssueStage" src/issues/types.ts && grep -Eq "export type IssueStatus" src/issues/types.ts && grep -Eq "blockedBy: string\[\]" src/issues/types.ts]

userStories.title: Pure graph helpers: isBlocked, deriveBlocks, referential-integrity check
userStories.description: As the issue system, I need pure, fully-tested graph helpers so that 'blocked' is computed from blockedBy (never stored) and dependency references are validated, without any I/O.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/issues/graph.ts exports `isBlocked(issue: IssueEntry, backlog: IssueEntry[]): boolean` returning true iff any id in `issue.blockedBy` resolves to a backlog entry whose `stage !== 'shipped'` (an unresolvable/missing id is treated by the referential-integrity check, not here: isBlocked considers only present, non-shipped deps as blocking). [oracle: grep -Eq "export function isBlocked" src/issues/graph.ts]

graph.ts exports `deriveBlocks(backlog: IssueEntry[]): Map<string, string[]>` building the reverse index (for each id, the list of issue ids that list it in their blockedBy). `blocks` is never stored, only derived. [oracle: grep -Eq "export function deriveBlocks" src/issues/graph.ts]

graph.ts exports a referential-integrity checker (e.g. `checkReferentialIntegrity(backlog): { ok: boolean; errors: string[] }`) that flags (a) any blockedBy id with no matching backlog entry and (b) any self-reference (an id listing its own id in blockedBy). Full cycle-rejection is OUT of scope (Epico C). [oracle: grep -Eq "export function checkReferentialIntegrity" src/issues/graph.ts]
All three helpers are pure (no Bun.file, no spawn, no fs, no git). [oracle: ! grep -Eq "Bun\.(file|spawn)|node:fs|node:child_process|spawnSync" src/issues/graph.ts]

Unit tests cover: isBlocked true when a dep is non-shipped, false when all deps shipped, false when blockedBy is empty; deriveBlocks reverse index correctness; referential-integrity flags a missing-id dep and a self-reference, and returns ok:true for a clean backlog. [oracle: bun test test/issues/graph.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full CI gate passes (bun run check:all -- the enforced spine that includes biome lint, typecheck, test, embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: NEW module src/issues/graph.ts; imports IssueEntry from src/issues/types.ts (US-001). MINIMAL graph for Epico A: only isBlocked + referential/self-ref checks. Do NOT implement Kahn topo-sort, cycle rejection, or escalation (those are Epico C, CAM-108, explicitly OUT of scope). Test file test/issues/graph.test.ts (mirror src path under test/).

userStories.title: Selection function selectPlannableIssue (the PRD-readiness gate)
userStories.description: As the cam-plan no-arg path, I need a deterministic, unit-tested function that returns the single plannable issue (or null) so that the PRD-readiness gate is a code invariant, not prose the orchestrator LLM interprets.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/issues/select.ts exports `selectPlannableIssue(backlog: IssueEntry[]): IssueEntry | null` that filters `stage === 'specified' && status === 'open' && !isBlocked(issue, backlog)`, sorts the survivors by `rank` ascending (entries with `rank` absent sort AFTER ranked ones) then by ascending numeric id (parsed from the id suffix after the last '-'), and returns the top candidate or null when none qualify. [oracle: grep -Eq "export function selectPlannableIssue" src/issues/select.ts]
Until rank exists (Epico C), the sort falls back to ascending numeric id: when no entry has a rank, ordering is purely by numeric id. [oracle: bun test test/issues/select.test.ts]

A thin deterministic resolver seam exists that the cam-plan prose can invoke as a one-liner (e.g. an exported helper `selectPlannableFromFile(cwd: string): IssueEntry | null` reading scripts/cam/issues.local.json via Bun.file/JSON.parse and delegating to selectPlannableIssue). The seam is the ONLY place the gate logic is duplicated for the prose; the pure function stays I/O-free. [oracle: grep -Eq "selectPlannableFromFile|export" src/issues/select.ts]

Unit tests assert the gate hard: idea/planned/shipped issues are invisible (never selected), abandoned issues are excluded, blocked issues are excluded, an empty/all-filtered backlog returns null, ranked entries sort before unranked, and ties by id are broken numerically (CAM-9 before CAM-12). [oracle: bun test test/issues/select.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full CI gate passes (bun run check:all -- the enforced spine that includes biome lint, typecheck, test, embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: NEW module src/issues/select.ts; imports IssueEntry (US-001) and isBlocked (US-002). This IS the D1 gate-as-code decision (ADR 0001 rejected 'convention not code'). SEAM CHOICE (justify in commit): prefer a small exported helper selectPlannableFromFile(cwd) over a new `cam` internal subcommand: the cam-plan prose already reads issues.local.json (it currently does it via `git show main:...` per the orchestrator-reads-from-main pattern in patterns.md), and a pure exported function keeps the gate testable without spawning a subprocess; a subcommand would add a CLI surface + thin-proxy dispatch overhead for zero gain. numeric-id parse: id.split('-').at(-1) is T|undefined under noUncheckedIndexedAccess, guard + Number() + Number.isNaN fallback. Test file test/issues/select.test.ts. Do NOT compute rank here (Epico C); only consume it if present. COVERAGE RATCHET (check:all per-story, CAM-60): scripts/coverage-budget.json floors are functions 75.65% / lines 78.63%. The selectPlannableFromFile I/O seam (Bun.file read) is deliberately thin -- keep it to a few lines so the well-tested pure selectPlannableIssue dominates the ratio, or add a tiny covering test, to avoid dipping the aggregate below the floor and failing check:all mid-implementation.

userStories.title: Idempotent migration script for the live issues.local.json
userStories.description: As the operator, I need a one-shot idempotent migration that rewrites every existing issue to the new schema (closed->shipped, open->idea, derive status, default blockedBy, drop priority) so the live backlog conforms without hardcoding counts, leaving the actual run on real data to the operator story.
acceptanceCriteria: A migration script (e.g. scripts/cam/migrate-issues-schema.ts) exposes a pure transform `migrateBacklog(raw: unknown): IssuesLocalJson` that maps each entry: old `state` in {closed,done,canceled} -> `stage:'shipped'`; old `state === 'open'` -> `stage:'idea'`; derives `status` (open->open; canceled/abandoned->abandoned; closed/done->open); sets `blockedBy: []` when absent; DROPS the ad-hoc `priority` field entirely; does NOT set wsjf/rank/spec. [oracle: grep -Eq "export function migrateBacklog" scripts/cam/migrate-issues-schema.ts]
The transform is generic over whatever is live (no hardcoded issue counts; iterates the actual issues array). [oracle: ! grep -Eq "(=|===) ?(31|37|105)\b" scripts/cam/migrate-issues-schema.ts]

Migration is idempotent: running migrateBacklog on an already-migrated backlog returns an equivalent backlog (re-run is a no-op; entries already at stage 'idea'/'shipped' with status set and no priority are left unchanged). [oracle: bun test test/issues/migrate.test.ts]

Tests run against fixtures that cover the priority drift (string 'P2', integer 2, and absent priority all dropped) and both old states (closed->shipped, open->idea), plus a canceled->abandoned case. [oracle: bun test test/issues/migrate.test.ts]

The script has a thin CLI entrypoint that, when run with a path, reads + transforms + writes the file via Bun.file, but the transform is the tested seam (the actual run on the real file is the operator story US-008, NOT this story). [oracle: grep -Eq "Bun.file" scripts/cam/migrate-issues-schema.ts]

Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full CI gate passes (bun run check:all -- the enforced spine that includes biome lint, typecheck, test, embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run check:all]

userStories.title: Run migration on the live backlog + dogfood the explicit-idea bridge
userStories.description: As the operator, I need to run the US-005 migration on the real scripts/cam/issues.local.json (after stopping concurrent writers), verify the closed->shipped and open->idea mapping, commit on main, then dogfood /cam-plan CAM-107 by id to confirm the D2 explicit-idea bridge works end to end.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent writers are stopped first (any live `cam run` sidecar writes issues.local.json via /cam-issue; multi-writer hazard) before mutating the file. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The US-005 migration is run on the real scripts/cam/issues.local.json: every previously-closed issue is now stage:'shipped', every previously-open issue is now stage:'idea' with status:'open' and blockedBy:[], and no entry retains a `priority` or `state` field. [oracle: bun -e "const d=await Bun.file('scripts/cam/issues.local.json').json(); for(const i of d.issues){ if(!['idea','specified','planned','shipped'].includes(i.stage)) throw new Error('bad stage '+i.id); if(!['open','abandoned'].includes(i.status)) throw new Error('bad status '+i.id); if('priority' in i) throw new Error('priority left on '+i.id); if('state' in i) throw new Error('state left on '+i.id); if(!Array.isArray(i.blockedBy)) throw new Error('no blockedBy '+i.id); }"]
The migrated file is committed on main (the backlog lives on main per the read-from-main invariant). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Dogfooding `/cam-plan CAM-107` by id produces a PRD for CAM-107 and prints the D2 'not grill-specified' warning (the explicit-idea bridge), confirming planning is unblocked during the Epico B transition. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

userStories.notes: OPERATOR CEREMONY (real data mutation + live-loop interaction): out of scope for autonomous implementation. Depends on US-005 (the migration script) and US-006 (the explicit-idea bridge in cam-plan). MULTI-WRITER HAZARD (patterns.md issues.local.json hygiene + memory): a live `cam run` sidecar is a concurrent writer of issues.local.json -- run `cam stop` (or stop the session) BEFORE running the migration, or the run loop will clobber the rewrite. After migrating: commit on main (read-from-main invariant). Then dogfood the D2 bridge by planning CAM-107 by id (the next epic). Operator flips passes:true manually and re-runs cam next.
